title: HCL: expressions, locals, type constraints and validation rules

videos.script: Ana's configuration works. It creates a VPC, and every value in it is typed out by hand. {{literal}} The shop now needs two subnets, the same tags on everything, and a dev network beside the prod one. Copying values around is how a typo reaches production. {{copies}} This lesson is about the language the files are written in, HCL. It is small. It has blocks, arguments and expressions, and very little else. {{blocks}} An expression can compute a value instead of stating it. A function can cut a range into subnets. A local can name the tags once, so every resource uses the same ones. {{compute}} Then the values coming in get a shape. A type says what a variable must look like. A validation rule says what it may contain. A wrong value stops the run before anything is created, with a sentence you wrote. {{rules}} You will try most of it in the console first, where an expression answers straight away. {{console}}
